title: Measures to Ease Singapore into Further Reopening after COVID-19 Circuit Breaker
what_it_is: Measures to Ease Singapore into Further Reopening after COVID-19 Circuit Breaker

sections.label: Return to workplaces from September 2020
sections.summary: From 28 September 2020 more work-from-home employees could return to workplaces, but at least half their working time must still be at home and no more than 50% at the workplace at any time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: From 28 September 2020, we allowed more employees who have been working from home to return to their workplaces, which Mr Louis Chua had asked about.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: However, we need to continue to keep our workplaces safe and minimise crowding.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Therefore, such employees should still continue to work from home for at least half their working time and there should be no more than 50% of such employees at the workplace at any point in time.

sections.label: Weddings and worship event limits
sections.summary: Up to 100 persons may attend weddings and religious events, in multiple zones or time slots of at most 50 persons each.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: We recognise the importance of key life events such as weddings and the importance of religious activities and worship to our spiritual needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Therefore, we have allowed greater numbers of up to 100 persons to attend each of these events, in multiple zones or time slots of at most 50 persons each to limit potential risk exposure.

sections.label: Road map towards Phase Three
sections.summary: The MTF is working on a road map towards Phase Three and will share more details in the coming weeks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: The MTF is working on a road map towards Phase Three and we will share more details when we are ready in the coming weeks.

sections.label: Flexible work-from-home arrangements
sections.summary: Because some homes are not conducive for working from home, employers and employees were given flexibility to work out arrangements, subject to no more than 50% of such employees at the office and not more than half their time in the workplace.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Some employees' homes may not be conducive for working from home.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Therefore, we made some arrangements and provided flexibility to allow the employers and the employees to work out better, more flexible arrangements, but subject to the criteria that I have just mentioned – no more than 50% of all employees who are working from home today, can go back to the office; and for those who are working from home today, not more than half of their time should be spent in the workplace; and they should still continue to work from home if they can.

sections.label: Continued flexible working after pandemic
sections.summary: Even after the COVID-19 pandemic is over, flexible working arrangements will continue to be encouraged.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: As I had mentioned in my reply, even after the COVID-19 pandemic is over, whenever that happens, we will continue to encourage this flexible working arrangement.

sections.label: DORSCON Orange review and employment practices
sections.summary: The speaker notes Singapore has been in DORSCON Orange since 7 February and asks whether the Government will review it, while employment practices work with MOM and MTI to engage stakeholders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: One specific measure would be relating to the DORSCON status.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I note that we have been in DORSCON Orange since 7 February earlier this year, and remain in DORSCON Orange today, even though the number of cases has gone from about more than 1,000 a day, to right now, less than 10.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Is that something which the Government will review in order to provide us with a more handy reference guide in terms of where we stand in the risk assessment?

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: For employment practices, we are working very closely with MOM and MTI to engage the various stakeholders.

sections.label: Maintaining DORSCON Orange
sections.summary: DORSCON Orange will be maintained until the global situation is under control, as cases elsewhere are still rising.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: At this moment, particularly, we have to be very mindful that while the number of cases in Singapore is low, the cases around us, in other parts of the world, are still rising.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: I will continue to maintain DORSCON Orange for the time being until we are quite confident that the global situation is under control.

sections.label: Global safety and Singapore
sections.summary: Singapore will not be safe until the world is safe.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Suffice to say that until the world is safe, we will not be safe.
